newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Post-communist Romania on right path-US official.
newsitem.headline: Post-communist Romania on right path-US official.

text.p: Romania is overcoming the handicap of decades of communist rule and is on the right path for joining NATO and other Western institutions, a senior U.S. official said on Saturday.
Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum told Reuters after talks with Foreign Secretary Andrei Severin that the Cold War had kept Romania out of Europe's main stream.

"Romania, as a number of other countries, suffered under the division of Europe," U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum told Reuters after talks with Foreign Minister Adrian Severin and other officials.

"One of the United States' most important goal is to make sure that this main stream develops through the continent. It is very important that a country like the U.S. understand the debt we have to countries like Romania."
Kornblum was holding two days of meetings with Romania's new centrist leaders after their victory over ex-communists in last November's general and presidential elections.
Neither he nor Severin disclosed details of discussions on Romania's bid to join NATO.

In a statement distributed by the U.S. embassy before his meeting with Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, Kornblum praised Romania's democratic progress and said it played a stabilising role in the Balkans.

"Romania and its people have shown a political maturity that bodes well for relations between Romania and the United States and for Romania's quest to enter into NATO and other Euro-Atlantic structures," the statement said.
"Romania is clearly on the right path."
Romania is a longshot for admission in the first wave of NATO expansion, to be announced at a July summit in Madrid.
But, along with Slovenia, it has made up ground in recent weeks on favoured Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic.

Western officials say the election of centrists committed to market reforms has helped Romania's case, along with signature of a political treaty with Hungary and renewed efforts to sign a similar document with Ukraine.
